# omadafusion_dhcp_reservation (Resource)

A DHCP reservation on a gateway-served LAN network (Services > DHCP Reservation). Reservations are keyed by MAC address. A client moves to its new address only after its lease renews.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "omadafusion_lan_network" "devices" {
  name = "Devices"
}

resource "omadafusion_dhcp_reservation" "printer" {
  mac         = "aa:bb:cc:11:22:33"
  ip          = "192.168.30.10"
  network_id  = data.omadafusion_lan_network.devices.id
  description = "Front desk printer"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `ip` (String) Reserved IPv4 address. Must be inside the network's subnet.
- `mac` (String) Client MAC address. `aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff` and `AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF` are both accepted.
- `network_id` (String) LAN network ID, e.g. from `data.omadafusion_lan_network`.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Free-text description shown in the controller.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the reservation is active. Defaults to `true`.
- `export_to_ip_mac_binding` (Boolean) Also export the pair to the gateway's IP-MAC binding table. Defaults to `true`.
- `site` (String) Site name or ID. Defaults to the provider `site`. Changing it forces a new resource.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The reserved MAC address, in `AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF` form.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <mac> or <site>/<mac>
terraform import omadafusion_dhcp_reservation.printer Default/AA-BB-CC-11-22-33
```
